headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP overlap: ECC can write shared state while OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/REST inputs, creating injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can write files, use MCP, and has shared session/state surfaces; OpenBBTerminal also uses MCP and stdin/stdout, so a content-to-instruction bridge is plausible. The pair lacks direct documented provenance controls, but the interaction is inferred rather than proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ECC writes attacker-controlled text into shared MCP or workspace files that OpenBBTerminal later parses as instructions
IF both agents are connected through the same MCP server or message channel without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate MCP servers per agent
Disable automatic parsing of file contents as instructions
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Review shared workspace files before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message schemas

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. ECC can read/write filesystem and network egress is allowlisted; OpenBBTerminal exposes APIs and MCP. A shared workspace could leak sensitive financial or operational data across the pair.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or Python environment
IF ECC reads files containing financial or licensed data that OpenBBTerminal stores or emits
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Restrict ECC access to non-sensitive folders
Mount OpenBBTerminal data read-only where possible
Rotate or redact shared logs after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, shell, and subprocess capabilities; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and exposes APIs, so both can mutate shared resources if co-located. ECC explicitly warns about separate roots to avoid overwriting session files, indicating real collision risk. The pairwise overlap is dangerous by default when sharing state.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, git repo, or MCP-backed mutable resource
IF OpenBBTerminal and ECC are run under the same OS user without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Disable git writes for one agent during shared runs
Serialize access with a lock file
Run each agent under a separate OS user
requires-engineering: add resource-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and modify code, docs, and security findings, while OpenBBTerminal consumes data through APIs and MCP. If OpenBBTerminal treats ECC output as authoritative, errors can propagate into financial analysis or downstream actions. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps it at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests ECC-produced files or summaries without verification
IF ECC-generated findings are used as inputs to financial models or API calls
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Compare outputs against source data
Mark ECC outputs as untrusted by default
Keep generated artifacts separate from live inputs
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session data, hooks, and security findings, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. Their documented data classes suggest a compliance mismatch risk if regulated financial data is mixed with ECC's broader developer-tool telemetry or retained in shared logs. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored in ECC session files or logs
IF retention or deletion policies differ for the same shared dataset
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ECC logs
Set short retention on shared artifacts
Separate audit trails by agent
Review data handling notices before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
